sources_considered.why: Primary research summary quantifies usable human-text supply, projected demand, and possible alternatives.
Dated primary audit documents increasing restrictions on training-data sources.
Dated experimental research provides material counterevidence to treating synthetic-data failure as inevitable.

evidence_items.locator: Section 'Results', paragraph describing the combined projection
evidence_items.explanation: This was evidence available in June 2024 of a prospective constraint on continued scaling with human-generated public text. The study also increased its supply estimate relative to earlier work and discussed alternatives, so it does not establish present exhaustion or an unavoidable halt.

evidence_items.locator: Abstract, sentence on Terms of Service restrictions
evidence_items.explanation: The longitudinal audit adds evidence that access to training material was becoming more restricted. Restrictions affect usable supply if respected or enforced; they do not mean the underlying text has disappeared.

The experiments identify circumstances in which retaining data while adding generated data avoids collapse. This is a material qualification, but does not demonstrate an unlimited supply of useful data for continued frontier scaling.

unresolved_gaps: These studies do not establish when every frontier developer would encounter a binding data constraint.
They do not settle how far synthetic data, other modalities, or greater data efficiency could extend scaling.
